newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Liberia elections to gulp $13 million - agency.
newsitem.headline: Liberia elections to gulp $13 million - agency.

text.p: Liberia's legislative and presidential elections scheduled for May 30 will cost about $13 million, Nigeria's state-run news agency reported on Sunday.
It quoted a Nigerian foreign ministry official as saying in the capital Abuja on Saturday that details of the cost were compiled by Liberia's seven-member electoral commission.

The expenditure had been passed on to Nigerian ruler General Sani Abacha in his capacity as chairman of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the official said, adding: "ECOWAS leaders would determine how to fund the exercise and we also hope on those who had pledged contributions.
"We are seeing the light at the end of the tunnel and it would be risky to lose the present momentum in implementation of the peace plan," he said.

The commission is yet to announce a formal election timetable but officials say nine parties had registered to present candidates for the polls, part of a peace plan brokered by West African countries and backed by Nigerian-led West African peace-keeping force ECOMOG.

Those that have entered for the presidential race include a woman Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf, former U.N. Development Programme Africa director, Charles Taylor, the man who launched the civil war in 1989 which has killed more than 150,000 people, and rival faction leader Alhaji Kromah.

The war has also displaced as many as half of Liberia's pre-war population of 2.5 million while several hundred thousand have turned refugees in neighbouring Ivory Coast, Guinea and Sierra Leone. Freed American slaves founded Liberia in 1847.
